title: Finite-dimensional compactifications and bounded-below restriction of etale adjunctions
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:V\to W$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$, $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ and $\eta_T:\mathrm{id}\to U_TS_T$ for site comparison and its derived unit [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback].

A compactification $c=(V\xrightarrow{j}\overline V\xrightarrow{p}W)$, with $j$ open and $p$ proper, exists [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The schemes $V,W$ and every such $\overline V$ are Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) and quasi-separated (the intersection of two affine opens is quasi-compact) [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]; $\overline V$ is finite type over $k$ and admits an integer dimension bound $d_c\ge0$, with $d_c=0$ allowed when $\overline V$ is empty [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. There is an ambient ordinary etale adjunction $F_c\dashv R_c$. Both $F_c$ and $R_c$ preserve $D^+$, the full subcategory of complexes with cohomology zero below some integer. The ambient Hom bijections restrict to an adjunction $F_c|_{D^+}\dashv R_c|_{D^+}$, whose unit and counit are the ambient ones under the full inclusions.

Moreover, for arbitrary $C\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $b\in\mathbf Z$ one has
$$S_VC\in D^{\ge b}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\in D^{\ge b}.$$
For $L\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the canonical map
$$S_VR_c(\eta_{W,L}):S_VR_cL\xrightarrow{\sim}S_VR_cU_WS_WL$$
is an isomorphism of bounded-below objects. No initial boundedness hypothesis on $R_cL$ is imposed.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is finite and commutative by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], clause 4. Its additive group is torsion: multiplication by its finite cardinality annihilates every element, hence every $A$-module sheaf. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps of $V,W$, then [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to the separated finite-type map $h$, giving a compactification $c$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated; compactification supplied by thm-nagata-compactification.

proof.text: For any compactification $c=(j,p)$, properness of $p$ includes finite type. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $\overline V\to W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] to $\overline V$. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] it has finite dimension. Choose a nonnegative integer bound $d_c$; if $\overline V$ is empty, choose $d_c=0$ (there are no chains of points to bound). This proves the geometric assertions for every compactification, without assuming that $j(V)$ is dense.

source.place: Finite-dimensionality assertion; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 and properties.tex Tag 01OY for Noetherianity and quasi-separatedness.

proof.text: For this $c$, [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] applies: $A$ is finite commutative, all three schemes are Noetherian, $j$ is open and $p$ is proper of finite type. Thus the ambient ordinary etale functor $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ has a right adjoint $R_c$. This is the ordinary module-sheaf adjunction, without any constructibility or pro-etale ambient-adjoint hypothesis.

source.place: Statement and Brown representability argument (Stacks Tag 0F5Y).

proof.text: The existing bounded-below compact-support functor is a functor between D+ categories. Its compatibility isomorphism with the ambient functor is rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusCompatibility, assembled from exact extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and unbounded/plus right-derived compatibility [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility]. Transport the boundedness property of its value along that isomorphism. No separate negative-cohomology calculation is needed.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing; exact extension by zero: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ; unbounded/plus compatibility: src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility.

proof.text: The field D.k is algebraically closed by IsAlgClosure.isAlgClosed, hence separably closed. Apply [lem-kun-relative-torsion-direct-image-dimension-bound] to the proper factor p with a_X=p followed by a_W and dimension bound d. The library comparison H^q(R+ p_* M[0]) isomorphic to the classical R^q p_* M gives vanishing in every natural degree q>2d. Apply [lem-etale-derived-functor-upper-amplitude], with the standard Grothendieck, injective-resolution and K-injective-resolution instances already provided for fixed-coefficient module sheaves by the adopted derived-category library. Exact extension by zero preserves upper bounds by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Thus F_c sends D^{<=m} into D^{<=m+N}, N=2d, on arbitrary unbounded input. For L in D^{>=b}, test R_c L against K in D^{<=b-N-1}. Adjunction identifies each map K to R_c L with a map F_c K to L. The latter is zero by t-structure orthogonality, since F_c K belongs to D^{<=b-1}. Orthogonality characterizes D^{>=b-N}, so R_c L belongs to it. This is the fixed-compactification version of the elementary argument of the former chosen-compactification amplitude interface; no transport to a chosen compactification is needed.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, (4)(c); upper-amplitude interface and the torsion relative dimension bound as stated in the cited DAG nodes.

proof.text: For $K\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, both $F_cK$ and $R_cL$ lie in the indicated full subcategories by steps 4–5. Consequently the same ambient bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F_cK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_cL)$ is a bijection of the subcategory Hom sets. Its naturality equations are the ambient equations. The unit is the transpose of $1_{F_cK}$ and the counit is the inverse transpose of $1_{R_cL}$, so the full inclusions send them to the ambient unit and counit, respectively. Their triangle identities are the same equations. This constructs the asserted restricted adjunction.

proof.text: The fixed-coefficient comparison inverse image already has exactness and faithfulness instances in the adopted source library (the exactness and full faithfulness assertions of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]). Use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]: its mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso identifies each derived cohomology sheaf after comparison with comparison of the original cohomology sheaf. The proved generic faithful-exact-functor lemma isZero_homologyFunctor_of_isZero_homologyFunctor_mapDerivedCategory_obj reflects vanishing by faithfulness; the exact-functor bound lemma preserves it. Apply the characterization of IsGE by vanishing in every degree i<b. This proves the equivalence for arbitrary C, with no lower boundedness assumption. The extra scalar-extension normalization clauses of lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact are unused: its specialized module need not be imported because the exactness instances are already supplied by the adopted comparison construction.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6, together with exact comparison inverse image (lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact); degreewise detection of zero.

proof.text: For L in D+, apply the existing unbounded canonical-unit theorem isIso_derivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_app, the ordinary fixed-coefficient form of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], at the underlying bounded-below object. Its target is bounded below by transport along this very unit isomorphism. The boundedness of R_c from step 5 and exact comparison from step 7 put both S_V R_c images in D+. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so applying S_V R_c to the specified unit gives precisely the required invertible morphism.
